policies.title: SSH daemon allows direct root login with a password
policies.description: Checks that root cannot log in over SSH with a password.
policies.rationale: A shared, well-known account name with full privileges is the first target of password guessing.
policies.absence_note: Default is prohibit-password (key-only for root) per the public man page, which is acceptable.
policies.remediation: Set PermitRootLogin to no (or prohibit-password) and use named accounts with sudo.

policies.title: SSH password authentication is enabled
policies.description: Checks that only key-based (or other strong) authentication is used.
policies.rationale: Passwords on an internet-reachable daemon invite brute force and credential stuffing.
policies.absence_note: Default is yes, so an absent line means passwords are accepted: treated as a failure.
policies.remediation: Set PasswordAuthentication no after confirming key logins work.

policies.title: SSH permits accounts with empty passwords
policies.description: Checks that accounts without a password cannot log in.
policies.rationale: An empty password turns the account into an open door.
policies.absence_note: Default is no per the public man page.

policies.title: SSH X11 forwarding is enabled
policies.description: Checks that X11 forwarding is off on servers.
policies.rationale: Forwarding exposes the client display to the server and the server to the display.
policies.absence_note: Default is no per the public man page.
policies.remediation: Set X11Forwarding no unless a documented need exists.

policies.title: SSH allows many authentication attempts per connection
policies.description: Checks that MaxAuthTries is 4 or lower.
policies.rationale: Fewer attempts per connection slows online guessing (this threshold is this project's own choice).
policies.absence_note: Default is 6 per the public man page, above the threshold used here: treated as a failure.

policies.title: SSH host-based authentication is enabled
policies.description: Checks that trust based on the client host (rhosts-style) is not used.
policies.rationale: Host trust lets one compromised machine impersonate every user on it.
policies.absence_note: Default is no per the public man page.

policies.title: SSH lets users set environment variables
policies.description: Checks that user-controlled environment settings are ignored.
policies.rationale: The man page notes this can bypass restrictions, for example through LD_PRELOAD.
policies.absence_note: Default is no per the public man page.

policies.title: SSH logging verbosity is not INFO or VERBOSE
policies.description: Checks that logging is neither suppressed nor at privacy-violating debug levels.
policies.rationale: QUIET/ERROR hides probing; DEBUG levels log more than the man page recommends.
policies.absence_note: Default is INFO per the public man page.
policies.remediation: Set LogLevel VERBOSE (records key fingerprints) or INFO.

policies.title: SSH honours .rhosts files
policies.description: Checks that legacy rhosts trust files are ignored.
policies.rationale: Rhosts files are an old trust mechanism that is easy to abuse.
policies.absence_note: Default is yes (UNVERIFIED in this research: not read from the man page).

policies.title: SSH idle sessions are never probed or closed
policies.description: Checks that ClientAliveInterval is between 1 and 900 seconds.
policies.rationale: Abandoned sessions stay usable by anyone who reaches the terminal.
policies.absence_note: Default ClientAliveInterval is 0 (no probes) per the public man page: treated as a failure.

policies.title: SSH login grace time is long or unlimited
policies.description: Checks that unauthenticated connections are dropped within 60 seconds (only plain seconds are understood).
policies.rationale: Long grace periods let idle unauthenticated connections tie up connection slots.
policies.absence_note: Default is 120 seconds (UNVERIFIED in this research), longer than the 60 s used here: treated as a failure.

policies.title: SSH offers legacy ciphers
policies.description: Checks that an explicit Ciphers line does not enable CBC, 3DES, RC4-family ciphers.
policies.rationale: These ciphers have known structural or key-size weaknesses.
policies.absence_note: Default cipher list favours ChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-GCM/CTR per the public man page (it still lists some legacy ciphers as supported, not default).
policies.remediation: Use an explicit modern list such as chacha20-poly1305, aes256-gcm and aes128-gcm.

policies.title: SSH offers legacy MACs
policies.description: Checks that an explicit MACs line does not enable MD5, truncated SHA-1 or 64-bit UMAC.
policies.rationale: Short or MD5-based MACs give weaker integrity protection.
policies.absence_note: Default MAC list favours encrypt-then-MAC variants per the public man page.

policies.title: SSH offers SHA-1 based key exchange
policies.description: Checks that an explicit KexAlgorithms line does not enable SHA-1 Diffie-Hellman groups.
policies.rationale: SHA-1 based exchanges and the 1024-bit group are considered legacy.
policies.absence_note: Default KEX list is modern in current OpenSSH (UNVERIFIED in this research).
policies.remediation: Use curve25519-sha256 and diffie-hellman-group16-sha512 or stronger.

policies.title: SSH StrictModes is disabled
policies.description: Checks that sshd refuses keys in files with unsafe ownership or permissions.
policies.rationale: Without it, a group-writable authorized_keys can be silently edited by others.
policies.absence_note: Default is yes (UNVERIFIED in this research).

policies.title: SSH protocol 1 is enabled
policies.description: Checks that a legacy Protocol line does not enable SSH-1.
policies.absence_note: Modern OpenSSH has no protocol 1 and no Protocol keyword (UNVERIFIED); absent means protocol 2 only.
policies.remediation: Remove the Protocol line or set Protocol 2.

policies.title: SSH has no user or group allow-list
policies.description: Checks that SSH access is limited to named users or groups.
policies.rationale: An allow-list limits exposure from forgotten or service accounts.
policies.absence_note: Without AllowUsers/AllowGroups every valid account may log in: treated as a failure.
policies.remediation: Add AllowGroups ssh-users (or AllowUsers) listing who may log in.
